parts.title: Campus Conversation: Signing Up for a Tutor
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and a tutoring center employee.
Student
Hi, I'd like to sign up for a tutor. I'm having trouble with my chemistry class.
Tutor
Sure. Is it a problem with homework, or are you preparing for an exam?
Student
Both, really. I have a midterm exam in two weeks, and I don't understand the lab reports.
Tutor
Okay. We have a chemistry tutor named Mr. Davis. He is available on Tuesday afternoons and Thursday mornings.
Student
I have a class on Thursday morning, so Tuesday is better. What time?
Tutor
He starts at two o'clock. Each session is one hour, and it's free for students.
Student
Free? That's great. Do I need to bring anything?
Tutor
Yes. Bring your textbook, your notes, and any lab reports you want to review.
Student
Okay. Actually, I might be a few minutes late next week because my class ends at one fifty.
Tutor
That's fine. The tutoring center is in the same building as your class, on the second floor.
Student
Perfect. Then I'll see him next Tuesday.
Tutor
Great. I'll put your name on the list.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Narrator
Listen again to part of the conversation. Then answer the question.
Student
Actually, I might be a few minutes late next week because my class ends at one fifty.

parts.title: Biology Lecture: How Octopuses Stay Safe
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Professor
Today we will talk about the octopus. The octopus is a very interesting animal because it can change its color in a few seconds.
Professor
Why does it do this? The main reason is protection. If a hungry fish comes near, the octopus changes color to match the rocks or sand around it. Then the fish cannot see it.
Professor

How does the color change work? The octopus has thousands of tiny cells in its skin called chromatophores. Each cell holds a colored liquid. When muscles pull on the cell, the color spreads out and becomes visible.
Professor
The octopus has a second way to stay safe. If it is in danger, it shoots a cloud of dark ink into the water. The fish cannot see well, and the octopus swims away.
Professor
Scientists are also surprised by its intelligence. An octopus can open a jar to get food inside. Some octopuses have even escaped from aquariums at night.
Professor
Interestingly, most octopuses are colorblind, so scientists still do not fully understand how they match colors so well.
Professor
To review: first, the octopus uses color change to hide; second, it uses ink to escape; and third, it is very intelligent.
Narrator
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Narrator
Listen again to part of the lecture. Then answer the question.
Professor
Interestingly, most octopuses are colorblind, so scientists still do not fully understand how they match colors so well.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.exp: The professor explains color change and ink.
They are tiny cells in the skin with colored liquid.

questions.q: What does the octopus do when it is in danger?
questions.exp: It shoots a cloud of ink.

o: Opening a jar to get food
questions.exp: An octopus can open a jar.

o: To say octopuses are not smart
To show that something is still a mystery
To change the topic to fish
questions.exp: He says most octopuses are colorblind, which is surprising.

o: He tells a story about an aquarium
He gives ways the octopus stays safe, then talks about intelligence
He lists only the history of octopus research
